title: 1993 AHSME Problem 25
statement: Let \(S\) be the set of points on the rays forming the sides of a \(120^\circ\) angle, and let \(P\) be a fixed point inside the angle on the angle bisector. Consider all distinct equilateral triangles \(PQR\) with \(Q\) and \(R\) in \(S.\) (Points \(Q\) and \(R\) may be on the same ray, and switching the names of \(Q\) and \(R\) does not create a distinct triangle.) There are

solutions.text: Let \(O\) be the vertex. Choose \(A\) on one ray so that \(OA=OP;\) because \(OP\) bisects the \(120^\circ\) angle, \(\triangle AOP\) is equilateral. For any \(Q\) on \(\overline{AO},\) choose \(R\) on the other ray with \(OR=AQ.\) Then \(\triangle POR\cong\triangle PAQ\) by SAS. Consequently \(PQ=PR\) and \(\angle QPR=\angle APO=60^\circ,\) so \(\triangle PQR\) is equilateral. Continuously many choices of \(Q\) give distinct triangles, hence certainly more than \(15.\) Thus the correct answer is E.
hints: Call the angle’s vertex \(O\) and choose \(A\) on one ray so that \(\triangle AOP\) is equilateral
Vary a point \(Q\) continuously on \(\overline{AO}\) and construct a matching point \(R\) on the other ray
